name: Balak
description: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness

points: Sacrificing animals was not solely a thing pertaining to Israel; sacrificing for sin is what pertained to Israel. All the ancient nations of old sacrificed animals when they worshipped their gods, so Balak and Balaam offering bullocks and rams on altars was nothing new to them.

note.label: Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed?

points: Balak the king of Moab brought Balaam from Aram to curse Jacob and defy Israel, and Balaam could not do it: how shall I curse, whom God hath not cursed?

note.label: Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed?

points: Balak's anger was kindled and he smote his hands together: I thought to promote thee unto great honour, but lo, the Lord hath kept thee back from honour. That was Satan speaking through Balak, trying to entice Balaam with honor to curse Israel.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

points: Balak's anger was kindled against Balaam because he wanted Balaam to curse us, and Balaam blessed us three times. Balaam said, If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the commandment of the Lord: Balaam knew it was the Lord sending that spirit upon him. Come, and I will advertise thee what this people shall do to thy people in the latter days.

Balaam answered: if Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the commandment of the Lord, to do either good or bad of mine own mind; but what the Lord saith, that will I speak.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

points: And Balaam rose up and returned to his place, and Balak also went his way; they parted.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

points: Then Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and warred against Israel, and sent and called Balaam the son of Beor to curse Israel; that is Numbers 22, read only days before this class.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: O my people, remember now what Balak king of Moab consulted, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him, that ye may know the righteousness of the Lord.
